key_highlights: ASX suffers fourth consecutive losing week as bond yields climb, pressuring equities broadly
RBA signals continued rate hikes despite sharp unemployment jump, creating an 'interest rate pincer' for households
AUD experiences sharp depreciation ('trapdoor opens'), raising import costs and commodity-linked equity risk
Australian house prices over halfway to largest 40-year decline; Victoria worst-hit on unemployment
Gold exploration sector active: Aurum 155g/t hit, Zenith 6/6 WA corridor hits, Auric high-grade beyond Munda pit shell
$2.7B cap raise torrent keeps ASX brokers busy, signalling small/mid-cap funding pressure
Intergenerational Report 2026 flags urgent tax reform need, adding fiscal policy uncertainty
Data centre boom straining energy supply, creating infrastructure and energy sector tailwinds

sectors.trend: Gold exploration names (Aurum, Zenith, Auric, Anax Metals, Many Peaks, MinRex) showing strong assay results; Rio2 drilling Peruvian copper; Vista Gold (VGZ) sale agreed. Gold sector outperforming amid AUD weakness and safe-haven flows.
sectors.implications: Gold miners and explorers benefit from AUD depreciation and rising yields. Copper exploration (Rio2) supports medium-term base-metals narrative. Small-cap cap raises ($2.7B) dilute existing holders but signal sector confidence.

sectors.trend: RBA hawkish stance despite unemployment spike supports net interest margins but pressures credit growth. Renters' financial stress (>50% struggling) raises NPL risk. Bond yield climb pressures bank valuations.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin tailwind vs credit headwind. Bond yield rise compresses equity multiples. Monitor NIM vs NPL trajectory.

sectors.trend: House prices over halfway to largest 40-year fall; CBD tower listed at $40m; Dusty Martin selling $20m portfolio. Victoria unemployment worst in nation. Renters' stress acute.
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX, SPG.AX) face occupancy and yield pressure. Residential developers (DHG.AX, LVH.AX) under stress. Defensive rotation away from property-linked equities.

sectors.trend: Data centre boom creating energy demand surge, straining grid supply. Energy security becomes policy priority.
sectors.implications: Energy names (SME.AX, WES.AX, AGL.AX) and grid/infrastructure plays benefit from structural demand. Potential government intervention in energy pricing.

sectors.trend: Interest rate pincer squeezing household budgets; >50% renters financially stressed. Consumer discretionary under pressure.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WTW.AX, IAG.AX face demand softness. Defensive staples (WOW.AX, CBA.AX) preferred. Consumer credit growth likely to decelerate.

sectors.trend: Global AI chip race intensifying (Nvidia, AMD, Intel, SK Hynix). Australian small-caps (Micro-X) in weekly runners. Data centre buildout supports local infrastructure.
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure but data centre energy demand benefits utilities. Micro-X.AX momentum play. Global AI capex cycle supports sentiment.

key_themes: RBA hawkish pivot vs rising unemployment creates stagflation risk
AUD depreciation amplifies commodity equity upside but raises import inflation
Bond yield climb pressuring equity valuations across ASX 200
Gold exploration sector in active discovery phase
Property market correction deepening, 40-year high drawdown
Intergenerational Report 2026 signals fiscal tightening ahead
Data centre energy demand as structural growth theme

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA continued hikes amid rising unemployment (stagflation)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight gold, energy, and defensive staples; underweight rate-sensitive property and consumer discretionary
Hedge AUD exposure; favour commodity exporters (BHP.AX, RIO.AX) with USD revenue; avoid import-heavy consumer names
Reduce REIT and residential developer exposure; monitor credit conditions at CBA.AX, NAB.AX

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Bond yield spike triggering equity de-rating
risk_assessment.mitigation: Shorten duration in bond portfolios; favour short-duration equities; monitor 10yr GSB yield
Monitor policy announcements; potential capital gains or super changes could shift sector flows
Avoid recent cap-raise names; favour well-funded explorers with low dilution history

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold exploration and production names
opportunities.rationale: Multiple high-grade hits (Aurum 155g/t, Zenith 6/6, Auric beyond Munda) plus AUD weakness and safe-haven demand create asymmetric upside

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy and grid infrastructure exposure
opportunities.rationale: Data centre boom creating structural energy demand; government likely to intervene, supporting regulated asset returns

opportunities.recommendation: Position in USD-revenue commodity majors as AUD hedge
opportunities.rationale: AUD depreciation directly boosts reported earnings for BHP, Rio Tinto; iron ore/coal demand resilient

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and residential property exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: 40-year house price decline underway; renter stress >50%; CBD listings signal oversupply

defensive_moves.recommendation: Shorten bond duration; favour short-dated GSBs
defensive_moves.rationale: RBA hiking cycle and yield volatility create capital loss risk in long bonds; 'will bonds crash stocks' risk elevated

defensive_moves.recommendation: Underweight consumer discretionary and rate-sensitive equities
defensive_moves.rationale: Interest rate pincer and renter stress suppress spending; unemployment rising in Victoria

market_outlook.short_term: ASX 200 likely to extend losses in 5th week as bond yields climb and RBA hawkishness persists. Gold and energy names outperform. AUD weakness supports miners but pressures importers. Volatility elevated.
market_outlook.long_term: Stagflation risk (hiking rates + rising unemployment) caps equity multiples. Property correction may extend 6-12 months. Gold and energy structurally supported. Tax reform from Intergenerational Report could shift sector flows in 2027. Recovery contingent on RBA pivot and credit stabilisation.
